theme: News and event databases: GDELT tooling, Google News scrapers, travel-industry news datasets (Skift, PhocusWire), regulatory news trackers
queries_run: gh search repos gdelt python --limit 30 --sort stars
gh search repos "gdelt events tourism" --limit 30 --sort stars
gh search repos "skift OR phocuswire" --limit 30 --sort updated
gh search repos "google news scraper" travel --limit 30 --sort stars
gh search repos "short-term rental" regulation tracker --limit 30 --sort stars
gh search repos gnews scraper --limit 20 --sort stars

candidates.name: gdelt-doc-api
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT-licensed, actively maintained (updated 11 Sep 2026) Python client for the GDELT 2.0 Doc API. Returns article-level search results, timeline volume, and timeline tone for any keyword/date-range query (e.g. 'Airbnb', 'short-term rental', 'vacation rental regulation') at daily granularity back to 2017. No committed dataset -- it is a live pull tool, but queries are date-bounded so a historical/point-in-time news-volume or tone series for Airbnb-relevant terms could be reconstructed after the fact.
candidates.why_useful: Directly addresses gap 14 (text/social -> GDELT) and partially gap 17 (nowcasting methods): a clean, current way to build a daily news-volume/sentiment index around Airbnb, STR regulation, or competitor mentions to test as a leading indicator for demand or regulatory shocks.
candidates.size_hint: no committed data; live API client

candidates.name: gdeltPyR
candidates.what_it_holds: 257-star, GPL-3.0 Python framework to retrieve full GDELT 1.0 and 2.0 Events tables (15-minute update cadence, back to 1979 for v1, 2015 for v2 events). Pulls raw event records (actors, event codes/CAMEO, geography, tone) into pandas, not just the Doc API subset.
candidates.why_useful: Lower-level than the Doc API client; would let a team filter GDELT Events by CAMEO codes/actor for tourism-, regulation-, or travel-related event categories (e.g. protest/legislation events tied to STR ordinances) rather than just keyword news volume. Addresses gap 14/17.
candidates.size_hint: no committed data; pull tool, GDELT itself is multi-TB

candidates.name: py-gdelt
candidates.what_it_holds: Small (4-star) but recently updated (8 Sep 2026) MIT-licensed comprehensive Python client covering GDELT Events, GKG, and Doc API endpoints in one package.
candidates.why_useful: Alternative/backup GDELT client if gdelt-doc-api or gdeltPyR prove insufficient; actively developed as of this week.

candidates.name: GDELT-GKG-Themes
candidates.what_it_holds: A committed CSV enumerating all known GDELT Global Knowledge Graph (GKG) theme codes (the taxonomy GDELT uses to tag articles, e.g. TOURISM, ECON_*, WB_*, TAX_* categories). Small reference file, not event data itself.
candidates.why_useful: Needed as a lookup table to filter GDELT GKG output for travel/tourism/hospitality/regulatory themes without guessing theme-code strings; a small but genuinely useful piece of plumbing for any GDELT-based nowcast.

candidates.name: GdeltForge
candidates.what_it_holds: Apache-2.0, recently updated (11 Sep 2026) tool that forges raw GDELT archives (Events, GKG, Mentions) into cleaned, reproducibly-sampled, cross-referenced Parquet files for downstream analysis.
candidates.why_useful: Could shortcut building a clean, joined Events+GKG+Mentions Parquet pipeline instead of writing one from scratch; useful plumbing for a GDELT-based travel/regulatory news nowcast.
candidates.time_coverage: depends on GDELT archive range pulled

candidates.name: es-gdelt
candidates.what_it_holds: Indexes the entire GDELT events database (including the 15-minute real-time feed) into Elasticsearch for query/aggregation.
candidates.why_useful: An alternative ingestion path if a searchable/aggregatable store of GDELT events is wanted instead of flat files; niche but functional (14 stars, still starred/updated recently for a 2025 repo).

candidates.name: Global-News-Intel-Platform
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT-licensed, actively updated (7 Sep 2026) end-to-end pipeline ingesting 100K+ daily GDELT events into MotherDuck/DuckDB with Dagster orchestration and a text-to-SQL chat interface, built to run at $0/month on free tiers.
candidates.why_useful: A ready-made low-cost orchestration pattern for standing up a continuously-updating GDELT store filtered to Airbnb/travel/STR-regulation keywords, if the team wants an ongoing news-event nowcast feed rather than one-off pulls.
candidates.size_hint: 100K+ events/day ingested, no historical backfill dataset committed

candidates.name: gdelt-downloader
candidates.what_it_holds: Python script to bulk-download GDELT GKG data with proxy rotation, weekday/hour filtering, resume capability, and file validation -- built for large/robust historical backfills.
candidates.why_useful: Practical for pulling a long historical GKG backfill (rather than the live Doc API's shorter-window queries) if a multi-year Airbnb/travel-news tone series is wanted; robustness features (resume, validation) matter for a multi-day bulk pull.

candidates.name: Eventdb-Validity-Audit
candidates.what_it_holds: Fully reproducible (R + Python) measurement-validity audit comparing four political-event databases (GDELT, ICEWS, Phoenix, Tsinghua) against a hand-built 712-event gold standard; finds GDELT tracks 'trade' events well but not 'opinion' events (Phoenix does opinion better). Includes the gold-standard dataset and comparison code.
candidates.why_useful: Not travel-specific, but directly relevant methodology if the team ever builds a GDELT-based news/event nowcast for ABNB: it is documented evidence of which event categories GDELT is and isn't reliable for, which should inform how much weight to put on a GDELT-derived signal.
candidates.time_coverage: gold standard sample period unspecified in listing, repo active as of 24 Aug 2026
candidates.size_hint: 712-event hand-coded gold standard + 4 event-DB comparison extracts

notes: Dead ends: no GitHub repos found for Skift or PhocusWire data/scrapers (searched 'skift OR phocuswire' with zero hits -- these are subscription trade-press sites with no evident open scraper or mirrored dataset on GitHub). 'Google news scraper' + travel and generic 'gnews scraper' searches returned only generic, non-travel-specific Google News scraping boilerplate (mostly 0-star student projects) -- excluded as not meeting the bar. 'short-term rental regulation tracker' search returned zero results on GitHub repo search; that gap (12) likely needs a different search angle (city-specific ordinance names, e.g. 'Local Law 18', 'HUTB', 'CITQ') better suited to a regulatory-themed scout. GDELT is the only real hit surface for this theme: several actively-maintained (Sep 2026) Python clients exist (Doc API, full Events, and combined clients), plus ETL/orchestration wrappers, but none are travel- or Airbnb-specific out of the box -- they are general-purpose tooling that would need keyword/theme filtering applied by us. No committed historical news datasets were found; everything in this theme is 'acquisition_method' rather than 'stored_dataset'. Suggest a follow-up scout try GitHub search directly for 'STR ordinance' / specific city regulation names, and another try 'Wayback Machine' + 'airbnb.com' archived-page tooling (gap 17) which this run did not have search budget to cover.
